reason: This text from Nehemiah describes Nehemiah's mission to rebuild Jerusalem's walls. While Nehemiah expresses personal distress about the city's ruined condition, he does not complain about the people. Instead, he rallies and encourages them, saying 'You see the distress we are in...Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, and we will no longer be in disgrace.' The people respond positively with 'Let us start building. So they strengthened their hands for the good work.' The only negative commentary comes from external enemies (Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem) who mock and deride the rebuilding effort—not from Hebrew leaders complaining about their own people.
